module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Latin Tableau Conjecture

The Latin Tableau Conjecture states that the graph associated
to any (finite) Young diagram (i.e., whose vertices are the
cells of the diagram, with edges between cells in the same row
or column) is CDS-colorable, meaning that there exists a proper
coloring of the vertices of the graph such that for all k > 0, the
number of vertices with color < k equals the maximum size of
the union of k independent sets of the graph.

*References:*

* [The Latin Tableau Conjecture](https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/view/v32i2p48)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace LatinTableau

variable {α : Type*} [DecidableEq α]

namespace SimpleGraph

/-- The Latin Tableau Conjecture: If G is the simple graph
  of a Young diagram, then G is CDS-colorable. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem LatinTableauConjecture (μ : YoungDiagram) :
     μ.toSimpleGraph.CDSColorable := by sorry

reformulations.difference: The source initially states the dominance criterion for existence of Latin tableaux of arbitrary shape λ and type μ. Lean instead asserts that every Young-diagram graph has one proper coloring whose first k color classes attain the maximum union size for every k.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The paper explicitly identifies CDS-colorability of every partition graph as equivalent to the conjecture (§2, Propositions 3 and 5 and Corollary 6). Writing α_k for the maximum union size, Lean's prefix equalities give color-class sizes α_(i+1) − α_i = δ_(i+1). Proposition 3 says this sequence is weakly decreasing for partition graphs, so the coloring has type δ. Conversely, a coloring of type δ can be relabeled starting at zero; telescoping then gives the required prefix equalities. Proposition 5 supplies tableaux of every type dominated by δ, recovering the full criterion; necessity follows from the definition of α_k. The use of potentially overlapping independent sets does not change α_k, since subtracting earlier sets makes them disjoint without changing their union. The additional k = 0 equation is automatically 0 = 0.

sources_consulted: Timothy Y. Chow and Mark G. Tiefenbruck, The Latin Tableau Conjecture, Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 32(2) (2025), #P2.48: §§1–2, Definitions 1–2, Propositions 3 and 5, Corollary 6, and §§4–5. https://www.combinatorics.org/ojs/index.php/eljc/article/download/v32i2p48/pdf
review.notes: Checked the sole theorem and its supporting YoungDiagram, graph, coloring, independence, cardinality, and supremum definitions. The cited paper treats the full conjecture as open and proves only partial results, so the category agrees with the source. /workspace/review/scratch.lean compiles without errors or warnings. It proves that the defining supremum is bounded and attained on finite graphs, proves equivalence with requiring disjoint independent sets, verifies the harmless k = 0 and empty-diagram cases, and proves CDS-colorability of the one-cell diagram. A proved finite computational version gives α-sequences [0,1,1], [0,2,3,3], and [0,2,4] for shapes (1), (2,1), and (2,2), respectively. The full dominance reformulation was checked against the paper, not reproved in Lean.
